newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says accepts French budget 1997 plan for EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU says accepts French budget 1997 plan for EMU.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it accepted French government plans to use money from state-owned France Telecom to help reduce the 1997 budget deficit in line with EU single currency requirements.
"Yves Franchet decided this morning to accept the French government proposal," a European Commission spokesman told a news conference.
Franchet, director general of EU's statistics office Eurostat, is responsible for the technical assessment of the French plan.

France regards the 37.5 billion franc ($7.35 billion) France Telecom transfer as vital in cutting its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product to qualify for the planned European single currency.
The payment would be in exchange for the French government assuming the state-owned telephone operator's pension liabilities.

Critics have said the one-off transfer smacked of creative accounting and ran counter to guidelines in the EU's Maastricht Treaty for countries to take sustainable economic measures to qualify for the planned 1999 start of the single currency.
On Tuesday, the franc fell against the mark after reports that an accounting working party had not approved the payment.
French finance ministry officials denied the report.

French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said on Wednesday he was confident of European Commission approval and quoted French President Jacques Chirac as pledging to cabinet colleagues that France would meet all deadlines in the drive to create a single European currency.
He said Chirac also said France and Germany would do everything that must be done to respect the calendar for European Economic and Monetary Union. ($=5.1 francs)
